_comment: Registry for the PRIORITY-EMPLOYER lane. Same entry shape as companies.json, plus three fields only this lane uses. These are employers the reader named explicitly — a referral, a recruiting contact, a deliberate target — so they are followed wherever she would actually work rather than only where she lives. Read only when settings.priority_search.enabled and a profile sets priority_search:true. The lane's geography is settings.location_priority (US-remote + Utah + Washington), NOT the Utah-only local gate. Every row here was probed live on 2026-08-25; see CLAUDE.md > Priority-employer lane for what each surface is and why it was chosen.
_fields_comment: priority:true stamps each posting so the discovery gate retrieves it on ONE signal instead of two (see classify_match) and the digest badges it. note is the reader's own sentence about the employer, rendered on the card verbatim — it is not a model judgment. exclude_titles drops titles this specific employer posts that she never wants; it is per-employer on purpose, because 'Director of Housekeeping' is a real leadership title that a profile-wide rule would have to keep. MATCHING IS WHOLE-WORD (the same \bterm\b rule as everywhere else in the engine), so write COMPLETE words: 'housekeep' silently matches nothing at all, 'housekeeping' and 'housekeeper' are what work.

companies.name: Adobe
companies.note: Referral network here: employee referral, recruiting contact, and a Women Tech Council connection. Apply through the referral, not the portal.
companies._comment: Adobe's tenant is 750 roles globally (38 pages, since Workday caps `limit` at 20), so it is scoped server-side. Lehi is deliberately ABSENT from search_texts: Adobe is already in companies.json with search_text 'Lehi', and the local lane covers it. Repeating it here would score the same Utah roles twice, once per lane snapshot. The companies.json row carries priority:true so those Lehi roles get the same relaxed retrieval.

companies.name: Salesforce
companies._comment: 1,530 roles globally = 77 pages unscoped. Note the host is myworkdaySITE, not myworkdayJOBS — the cxs path is otherwise identical. 'Washington' is NOT a search term: it returns Washington DC in bulk, and the WA city names are the precise cut.

companies.name: Zillow Group
companies._comment: 117 roles, small enough to page whole. www.zillow.com/careers/ answers 403 to any non-browser client; the Workday tenant behind it does not. Zillow labels remote roles 'Remote-USA', which is_us_remote reads correctly.

companies.name: Atlassian
companies._comment: One request for the whole board (~250 roles) with full prose. Its actual ATS is iCIMS (globalcareers-atlassian.icims.com), which has no public API — this endpoint is the supported surface.

companies.name: NPR
companies._comment: Plain Greenhouse board, ~14 roles. Most are Washington DC, which this lane's geography excludes by design (is_washington guards against DC), so in practice its Remote roles are what surface. exclude_titles drops production CRAFT only: 'Managing Editor', 'Director, Digital Insights' and every strategy/ops title still come through, which is the 'beyond media-production positions' ask.

companies.name: PBS
companies._comment: GOTCHA: `slug` here is the Workday TENANT and it is vhr_pbs with an UNDERSCORE, while the host is vhr-pbs with a hyphen, and wd5 (which the careers page also advertises) 422s — only wd115 answers. Tiny board, 8 roles.

companies.name: Marriott International
companies._comment: filter[brand][0]=Corporate is Marriott's OWN corporate/property split (337 corporate vs 12,900+ property), which is why this reads as 'corporate roles, not property-level operations' rather than us guessing from titles. is_remote is the reason Marriott is on Paradox and not on its Oracle tenant: Oracle has the same corporate cut but reports every one of its 13,301 requisitions as ORA_ON_SITE, so the remote roles would all be dropped as Bethesda-only. exclude_titles is belt-and-braces for property titles that leak into the corporate brand.

companies.name: Hilton
companies._comment: organizations = 'US Corporate/Executive' (81) + 'Hilton' (41), out of 4,390 total — the corporate cut, on Hilton's own classification. The EMEA/APAC corporate orgs (300005400802363 / 300005400802339) are deliberately left out as out-of-geography. Unlike Marriott, Hilton DOES populate WorkplaceType, so fetch_oracle folds Remote/Hybrid into the location and the gates see it.

_rejected_comment: Zillow's own careers page (www.zillow.com/careers/) 403s every non-browser client and is not needed. Marriott's Oracle tenant (ejwl.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com / MI_CS_1) works and is cheaper (2 requests for all 373 corporate roles vs ~10) but reports no work arrangement at all, so it cannot find the remote corporate roles that are the point. Marriott's Paradox page HTML server-renders only 10 results and ignores page_size, so the /api/get-jobs endpoint is the only sane surface. Salesforce and Adobe both cap Workday `limit` at 20 regardless of what is sent — do not try raising it again.
